title: Field Service Standard for Machine Faults on the Vending Services Program
content:
A fault reported on a Vending Services Program machine is logged as a service call against that machine, and the call carries the machine it concerns so that repeat faults on one machine can be seen. Calls are logged while the agreement stands active or suspended, since a suspended machine may still need attention before it is switched back on; the standing of the agreement and the machines it carries are read from the vending agreement record.

A logged service call is attended no later than the response window for the programme, counted in elapsed hours from the day the client logs the service call. Elapsed hours run continuously from the moment the call is logged, nights, weekends and public holidays included, and a visit made exactly on the boundary hour is in time; elapsed hours are never rounded up to whole calendar days.

Calls inside the included count printed against the programme for the agreement year carry no charge; calls beyond that count carry the call-out charge printed against the same programme. A call raised for a fault that turns out to be a power supply, a network or an access problem on the client's side is charged as a call-out whether or not the included count has been used up.

A machine standing out of service beyond the response window earns the daily outage credit printed against the programme for each further day, credited on the next statement.

A machine that has needed more than 6 calls in the rolling twelve months is replaced rather than repaired again, at no charge to the client. The count is of the calls logged on the agreement in the twelve calendar months ending on the day the call is logged.

### The response window at its boundary (hypothetical hours)

On a programme whose response window is 24 hours, a call logged at the middle of an afternoon is attended in time if the visit is made at any point up to and including the same hour of the following afternoon, because a visit made exactly on the boundary hour is in time. A visit made an hour later than that is outside the window. The hours run through the night and through a weekend without pause, so a call logged on a Friday afternoon is measured in the same continuous hours as one logged on a Tuesday morning, and the window is never converted into a count of whole calendar days. The window figure used here is an illustration of the counting.

### What a call is charged

| The call in question | What is charged |
| --- | --- |
| Inside the included count for the agreement year, machine fault | nothing |
| Beyond the included count for the agreement year, machine fault | the call-out charge printed against the programme |
| A client-side power supply, network or access problem, inside the included count | the call-out charge printed against the programme |
| A client-side power supply, network or access problem, beyond the included count | the call-out charge printed against the programme |

The outage credit is a separate matter from what a call is charged. It is earned by a machine that stands out of service beyond the response window, for each further day it so stands, at the daily figure printed against the programme, and it is credited on the next statement rather than set against the call.

### The replacement count on either side of its threshold

A machine that has needed 6 calls in the rolling twelve months has not needed more than 6, and is repaired as before. A machine that has needed 7 in that same rolling twelve months has needed more than 6, and is replaced rather than repaired again, at no charge to the client. The twelve months are counted back from the day the call is logged, so the count moves as the window rolls forward.
